key_facts: Topical corticosteroids ineffective in controlling symptoms
Physical examination revealed erythematous papules, crusts, and excoriations
Scales and fissures on the lower lip
Normal blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement
Skin biopsy showed spongiosis and erosions in the epidermis
Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis
CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells in the germinal center
Phototest with solar simulator showed delayed erythema to UV-A

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including generalized pruritus and erythematous papules, along with the presence of scales and fissures on the lower lip, are consistent with chronic actinic dermatitis. The phototest results showing delayed erythema to UV-A also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: The skin biopsy results, while showing a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate, do not specifically indicate mycosis fungoides, and the clinical presentation is not typical for this condition.

rejected.label: atopic dermatitis
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of other medical history make atopic dermatitis less likely, and the skin biopsy results do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The skin biopsy results, including the presence of CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells, do not specifically indicate cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, and the clinical presentation is not typical for this condition.
